buoy_reference._comment: BUOY trust-CHECK disposition. apply_nwps_assignments READS this block (pending[]/retired[]/unverifiable[]) alongside trust_by_zone to set each placed spot's nwps_direction_status — it is NOT inert. trust_by_zone stays the HEIGHT-tagging gate (whether a spot consumes NWPS). THREE states: (1) 'pending' — a VALID reference buoy exists; the spots are placed on NWPS HEIGHT now but direction is NOT yet buoy-verified (no swell has run --trustcheck), so the buoy is NOT PASS in trust_by_zone; the buoy-ready monitor WATCHES it and a qualifying swell accumulates a --trustcheck; direction is confirmed when the rolling verdict settles PASS. (2) 'retired' — NO valid nearshore reference buoy exists (e.g. 44098: a structurally-invalid 76 m offshore bank vs shallow nearshore nodes); the spots KEEP NWPS height + raycast direction on the listed 'axes'; the monitor EXCLUDES the buoy (never flagged). 'axes' is load-bearing: a record whose axes include 'direction' makes apply label those spots nwps_direction_status='unverifiable' (never 'verified') even when the buoy is PASS — that PASS is a HEIGHT verification only. (3) 'unverifiable' — a spot placed on NWPS HEIGHT (like pending, but with NO trust PASS and NO valid buoy on the row) whose direction can NEVER be buoy-verified: island-shadowed geometry where the nearest valid buoy is around a headland in different exposure. Keyed by SLUG; the row's nwps_buoy_id is null; the far 'nearest_candidate' is AUDIT-ONLY and is never used for placement or verification. apply checks unverifiable BEFORE the PASS branch, so these can never be relabeled 'verified'; the monitor NEVER watches them (no WATCH entry) and no far-buoy trust-check ever runs. Distinctions: pending = valid nearby buoy, awaiting a swell; retired = a buoy is nearby but structurally invalid; unverifiable = a valid buoy exists elsewhere but is geometrically wrong for these spots.
